lead: An isolated footing carries one column and spreads its load over enough soil to keep bearing pressure safe. The pad may be square, rectangular or circular in plan. It is sized from service load and safe bearing capacity, then designed for factored bending, one-way shear and punching shear. You see these footings under building columns, compound-wall piers and small industrial sheds.
prereq: You need: 5.2 for column load and bars, 5.4 for bearing pressure, and Unit 3 for shear and development length.

blocks.text: Start with service load P in kN and safe bearing capacity q<sub>s</sub> in kN/m². The plan area must satisfy A ≥ P/q<sub>s</sub>. For a square footing, side L = √A. For a rectangular footing, choose L and B so LB ≥ A, often with L/B between 1 and 2. For a circular footing, diameter D = √(4A/π). Round up to a practical size, usually a multiple of 50 mm.

Then add the footing self weight and check p = (P + W<sub>f</sub>)/A ≤ q<sub>s</sub>, where W<sub>f</sub> is self weight in kN. A quick first guess is W<sub>f</sub> = 0.1P. Use service loads for soil pressure and factored loads for concrete design.

For an eccentric column load, pressure is not uniform: p<sub>max</sub> = P/A + M/Z and p<sub>min</sub> = P/A − M/Z, where M is service moment in kN·m and Z is section modulus in m³. Keep p<sub>max</sub> ≤ q<sub>s</sub> and p<sub>min</sub> ≥ 0 so the soil does not lift. For a rectangular pad of sides L and B, bending about the axis parallel to B gives Z = BL²/6 in m³; use the axis about which the moment acts.

blocks.where: P is service column load in kN; q<sub>s</sub> is safe bearing capacity in kN/m²; A is plan area in m²; L is square side and D is circular diameter, both in m.

blocks.text: Use factored column load P<sub>u</sub> = 1.5P for concrete design. The net upward pressure is w<sub>u</sub> = P<sub>u</sub>/A in kN/m². For a square pad of side L and a square column of side c, the cantilever projection is l = (L − c)/2. Bending is checked at the column face, not at the pad edge. The moment per metre width is M<sub>u</sub> = w<sub>u</sub>l²/2. For a rectangular pad, take b as the column side parallel to L and c as the column side parallel to B, so l<sub>x</sub> = (L − b)/2 and l<sub>y</sub> = (B − c)/2 give moments in the two directions. For a circular pad, a simple first design treats a unit-width radial strip as a cantilever of length (D − d<sub>c</sub>)/2, where d<sub>c</sub> is column diameter.

Find effective depth from the limiting moment: M<sub>u,lim</sub> = 0.138 f<sub>ck</sub>b d² for Fe415 steel, with b = 1000 mm. So d = √(M<sub>u</sub> × 10⁶/(0.138 f<sub>ck</sub> × 1000)). Use 0.133 for Fe500 and 0.148 for Fe250. Then find steel from M<sub>u</sub> = 0.87f<sub>y</sub>A<sub>st</sub>d(1 − f<sub>y</sub>A<sub>st</sub>/(f<sub>ck</sub>bd)). Provide at least 0.12% of gross area for Fe415, and 0.15% for mild steel. Check both directions. The longer projection gives the larger moment per metre, so the direction of the longer side of the pad usually needs more steel; the shorter direction needs less.
w<sub>u</sub> = P<sub>u</sub>/A; M<sub>u</sub> = w<sub>u</sub>l²/2; d = √(M<sub>u</sub> × 10⁶/(0.138 f<sub>ck</sub> × 1000))
blocks.where: P<sub>u</sub> is factored column load in kN; A is plan area in m²; w<sub>u</sub> = P<sub>u</sub>/A is in kN/m²; l is the projection in m; M<sub>u</sub> = w<sub>u</sub>l²/2 is in kN·m per metre width (multiply by 10⁶ to get N·mm); f<sub>ck</sub> is in N/mm²; b is taken as 1000 mm and d comes out in mm.

blocks.text: One-way shear is checked on a vertical section at distance d from the column face. For a square footing, V<sub>u</sub> = w<sub>u</sub>L(l − d), with l = (L − c)/2. The stress is τ<sub>v</sub> = V<sub>u</sub>/(B d) ≤ τ<sub>c</sub>, where B is the width at that section and τ<sub>c</sub> is the concrete shear strength from Unit 3. If τ<sub>v</sub> exceeds τ<sub>c</sub>, increase the depth.

Punching shear is checked on a perimeter at d/2 from the column face. For a square column of side c, perimeter b<sub>0</sub> = 4(c + d) and inside area = (c + d)². The net punching force is V<sub>u</sub> = P<sub>u</sub> − w<sub>u</sub>(c + d)². The stress is τ<sub>v</sub> = V<sub>u</sub>/(b<sub>0</sub>d) ≤ k<sub>s</sub>τ<sub>c</sub>, where k<sub>s</sub> = 0.5 + β<sub>c</sub> ≤ 1 and β<sub>c</sub> is short side/long side of the column. For a square column, k<sub>s</sub> = 1. For a circular column, b<sub>0</sub> = π(d<sub>c</sub> + d).

Column bars must extend into the footing for development length L<sub>d</sub>. For M20 concrete and Fe415 steel, L<sub>d</sub> ≈ 47φ in tension. Provide at least that length below the column face. A sloped footing saves concrete, but its depth changes, so repeat bending, one-way shear and punching checks at each critical section.
b<sub>0</sub> = 4(c + d); V<sub>u</sub> = P<sub>u</sub> − w<sub>u</sub>(c + d)²; τ<sub>v</sub> = V<sub>u</sub>/(b<sub>0</sub>d) ≤ k<sub>s</sub>τ<sub>c</sub>
blocks.where: b<sub>0</sub> is punching perimeter in mm; c is square column side in mm; d is effective depth in mm; V<sub>u</sub> is net punching force in N; w<sub>u</sub> is net upward pressure; k<sub>s</sub> is 0.5 + β<sub>c</sub> but not more than 1.

figure.caption: The 1000 kN column load needs 5 m², so a 2.3 m square pad is adopted; the factored upward pressure w<sub>u</sub> is the same for the bending, one-way shear and punching checks (worked example covers sizing and bending depth only).

spec.title: Isolated footing checks
spec.aria: Flow from a 400 mm column and 1000 kN load to a 5 square metre required area, then to a 2.3 m square footing, then to bending, one-way shear and punching shear checks.

examples.question: An isolated square footing supports a 400 mm square column with a service load of 1000 kN. The safe bearing capacity is 200 kN/m². Use M20 concrete and Fe415 steel. Find the footing size and the depth required for bending at the column face. Take cover 50 mm and assume 16 mm bars.
steps: 1. Plan area: A = 1000/200 = 5.0 m². Side = √5.0 = 2.24 m. Adopt L = 2.3 m, so actual area = 5.29 m².
2. Self-weight check: assume 300 mm thickness. W<sub>f</sub> = 0.3 × 5.29 × 25 = 39.7 kN. p = (1000 + 39.7)/5.29 = 196.5 kN/m² < 200 kN/m². Safe.
3. Factored load: P<sub>u</sub> = 1.5 × 1000 = 1500 kN. Net pressure: w<sub>u</sub> = 1500/5.29 = 283.55 kN/m².
4. Projection: l = (2.3 − 0.4)/2 = 0.95 m. M<sub>u</sub> = 283.55 × 0.95²/2 = 127.95 kN·m per metre width.
6. Overall depth with 50 mm cover and 16 mm bars: D = 220 + 50 + 8 = 278 mm. Adopt 300 mm.
examples.answer: Adopt a 2.3 m × 2.3 m square footing, 300 mm thick, with effective depth 220 mm; the required depth for bending was 215.3 mm.
examples.check:
import math
P = 1000.0
q = 200.0
A = P/q
side = math.sqrt(A)
L = math.ceil(side*10)/10
Aact = L*L
t = 0.3
W = t*Aact*25
p = (P + W)/Aact
Pu = 1.5*P
wu = Pu/Aact
l = (L - 0.4)/2
Mu = wu*l*l/2
d = math.sqrt(Mu*1e6/(0.138*20*1000))
print(f"{A:.1f}")
print(f"{L:.1f}")
print(f"{Aact:.2f}")
print(f"{W:.1f}")
print(f"{p:.1f}")
print(f"{Pu:.0f}")
print(f"{wu:.2f}")
print(f"{l:.2f}")
print(f"{Mu:.2f}")
print(f"{d:.1f}")

traps: Punching shear is checked on the perimeter at d/2 from the column face, not on the column face. The column-face perimeter gives a much larger stress and is wrong.
Use service load and safe bearing capacity for sizing. Use factored load and net upward pressure for bending and shear. Mixing them is the commonest error.
Do not include the footing self weight in the net upward pressure for bending; it is balanced by soil reaction under the whole pad. Do include it in the bearing pressure check.
Effective depth is not overall depth. Subtract cover and half the bar diameter.
In a rectangular footing the two directions have different projections, so they have different moments per metre.

quiz.a: A pad under one column that spreads its load over soil.

quiz.q: What development length is needed for M20 Fe415 column bars?
Why are service loads used for bearing pressure and factored loads for bending?
quiz.a: Soil pressure is a serviceability check; concrete strength is a collapse check.

quiz.q: A 500 mm square column carries 1200 kN service load. q<sub>s</sub> = 150 kN/m². Find a square side, ignoring self weight.
A 2.5 m square footing has w<sub>u</sub> = 300 kN/m² and a 400 mm column. Find M<sub>u</sub> at the column face and d for M20 Fe415.
Find the punching perimeter and inside area for a 300 mm square column with d = 200 mm.
quiz.a: b<sub>0</sub> = 4(300 + 200) = 2000 mm. Inside area = (500 mm)² = 0.25 m².

quiz.q: Why does a sloped footing need more shear checks than a uniform pad?
quiz.a: Its depth changes, so each critical section has its own d and shear capacity.

beyond: Not for the exam. Design offices use finite-element or plate-on-elastic-foundation software for large or irregular footings. Research topics include soil-structure interaction, eccentrically loaded footings and ring footings for circular tanks. Search for “isolated footing punching shear”, “sloped footing design” and “elastic foundation plate”.
